eyebrowDiagnosis: A clearer picture of your connection
desktopOnly: Run the desktop app to read real network information.
readySummary: Scan 8 configuration areas to review findings and eligible repairs.
diagnosisHint: Diagnosis is read-only. Repair explains its impact and backs up restorable settings.
repairHint: Review the impact before repair. Restorable settings will be backed up.
selectRepairHint: Choose only what fits your setup, especially on work networks or VPNs.
restoreHint: Restore settings saved by this app
speedIntro: Measure single-connection throughput and HTTP round-trip time to Cloudflare.
systemProxyHint: Follow system proxy or PAC rules
trafficLimit: Up to about 73 MiB of payload and 30 seconds per test, plus protocol overhead. Consider metered data.
speedDisclaimer: Results describe only the path to this endpoint, not guaranteed ISP bandwidth. HTTP round-trip is not ICMP Ping.
advancedIntro: Use read-only tools to inspect name resolution, connectivity and routes.
outputEmpty: Results will appear here after you run a tool.
adaptersIntro: Read interface, address and link information reported by Windows.
infoEmpty: Select Refresh to read current system information.
connectionsIntro: A read-only snapshot of system connections. Their state can change at any time.
settingsIntro: Choose your language and the level of detail that suits you.
modeHint: Beginner provides scans and suggested repairs. Advanced opens a separate workbench for evidence and manual repair policies.
aboutBoundary: Configuration checks stay on this device. Connectivity checks and speed tests contact endpoints when you start them.
bridgeError: The desktop connection is unavailable. Reopen the app.
languageError: Local language resources could not be loaded. Check that app files are complete.
evidenceEmpty: This check has not run. Start diagnosis to view actual evidence.
scanSummary: Collecting configuration and connectivity evidence. You can stop this read-only check.
noRepairs: No targeted repair meets the current evidence. Review the findings to continue troubleshooting.
repairsAfterScan: Eligible repair actions appear here after diagnosis.
genericError: The operation did not finish. Review the details and try again.
hostError: Enter a hostname or IP address, without a URL, spaces or path.
portError: Port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535.
native.elevatePrompt: Repair needs administrator access. The app will reopen as administrator for this account and run diagnosis again. Select the repairs again afterward. Repairs will not run automatically.
native.crossAccount: Administrator approval switched to another Windows account. The operation stopped to avoid changing another account’s proxy or losing access to encrypted backups.
native.restorePrompt: Restorable settings in the backup will be applied and may briefly interrupt your connection. Current settings will be backed up first. Continue?
native.restart: A restart is needed to confirm the final result. This app will not restart your computer automatically.
native.nothing: No automatic repair is available for the current findings.
native.busy: Wait for the current task to finish.
native.noWebView: Unable to load the bundled interface component. Extract the complete portable package to a writable local folder and try again. Details: {0}
native.invalidMessage: The request is invalid or outside the allowed scope.
native.operationActive: Settings are being repaired. Wait for the operation to finish before closing.
native.advancedOnly: This feature is available in Advanced mode.
workbenchEmpty: Run diagnosis to review findings, evidence and repair policies in one workspace.
evidencePanelHint: Select a check to inspect its evidence. Diagnosis does not change settings.
repairBeforeHint: Eligible repair suggestions will appear after diagnosis.
repairScanningHint: Checking settings. Repair is unavailable until diagnosis finishes.
repairHealthyHint: All current checks passed. No automatic repair is needed.
repairManualHint: No automatic repair meets the safety conditions. Review the evidence or continue in Advanced mode.
repairRunningHint: Diagnosis will run again after repair. Keep the app open.
safeSelectionHint: Only recommended candidates are listed. Selected items will be confirmed and backed up before repair.
noSelectionHint: Recommended repairs are available. Select at least one to enable one-click repair.
selectedRepairsHint: Repair only selected items, after impact review and backup.
noConfirmedChanges: No confirmed configuration differences were recorded. This does not prove every setting remained unchanged.
historyEmpty: No repair history yet. Repairs and restorations will appear here.
historyReadError: History could not be read. The original file is preserved; network repair remains available.
historyWriteWarning: The operation finished, but its history could not be saved. Keep the backup location shown in the result.
noRestorableBackup: No readable local backup was found. You can select an existing backup in advanced mode.
monitorUnavailable: Sampling could not start. Check the target or name resolution.
monitorFinished: Monitoring ended. Collected data is shown below.
dnsNoRecords: A response was received with no address records for this type. Check its RCODE.
dnsNoAnswer: No verifiable DNS response was obtained. It may have timed out, been refused, or failed protocol validation.
dnsTcpFallback: The UDP response was truncated and retried over TCP.
monitorInputError: Enter a hostname or IP. Use a 1–10 second interval and 1–3600 samples.
dnsCompareInputError: Enter a valid hostname and 1–4 DNS server IPs separated by commas.
monitorIntro: Use web checks with the system proxy for VPN connections, or Ping to measure ICMP packet loss.
monitorChartHint: Shows the latest 300 samples; gaps indicate no response. Web timing includes DNS, TLS and proxy processing.
monitorChartEmpty: Actual samples will appear after monitoring starts.
dnsCompareIntro: Query A / AAAA records from selected resolvers. CDN answers commonly differ; differences alone do not prove DNS tampering.
dnsComparePrivacy: Queries the selected DNS servers directly, without the system HTTP proxy. Different answers can be caused by a CDN and do not prove DNS tampering.
historyIntro: The latest 100 entries are encrypted on this computer. Exports are redacted by default; backups stay local.
redactionReview: Exports hide common network identifiers using fixed rules. Review free text before sharing.
previewLimited: This preview is shortened. Export a redacted report for the complete record.
historyShowing: Shows the latest 20 entries. Exports include all locally retained entries.
redactionNotice: The report has been redacted using fixed rules. Review its free text before sharing.
simpleProxyFound: The proxy program is no longer running, but this computer is still using it.
simpleProxyImpact: Web requests cannot pass through this inactive proxy.
simpleProxyAdvice: Turn off the leftover proxy setting, then check the connection again. A backup is saved first.
simpleUncertain: This check could not confirm whether there is a problem.
simpleAdvice: Review the findings first. Apply a repair only when a suitable recommendation is available.
simpleNoRepair: No repair is needed for this item.
moreInAdvanced: Detailed diagnostic data is available in advanced mode.
simpleHardware: Check the network hardware and connection, including the cable, Wi-Fi and adapter.
simpleConnection: The computer's network address or gateway settings need checking.
simpleDhcpService: The service used to obtain a network address automatically needs checking.
simpleDns: Website address lookups did not produce normal results in this test.
simpleHosts: The computer's local website address mapping rules need reviewing.
simpleProxy: The computer's proxy settings need reviewing.
simpleWinsock: The system's network protocol components need further checking.
simpleHttp: Web access was not confirmed by this test.
impactDisableProxy: Turn off the current user's manual proxy. Apps relying on it may be affected. The proxy address is kept and the automatic proxy script is unchanged. The evidence is checked again and a backup is saved first.
impactFlushDns: Clear the Windows name-resolution cache without changing DNS servers, IP addresses or proxy settings. Cleared cache entries cannot be restored.
impactRenewDhcp: Request a fresh automatically assigned address for the selected adapter. The connection may briefly drop. A dynamic lease and address cannot be guaranteed to return to their previous values.
impactAutoDns: Set the selected adapter to obtain DNS automatically. Dedicated DNS for a company, campus or VPN may be affected. The previous settings are backed up first.
monitorWebHint: Fetches HTTPS response headers only. System rules may select a direct route; ignoring the HTTP proxy does not bypass a VPN adapter.
monitorIcmpHint: Ping does not use the system HTTP proxy. Some VPNs or websites do not respond to ICMP; try a web check if every sample fails.
monitorHttpMeaning: An HTTP response does not guarantee usable page content: 3xx is a redirect, and 4xx / 5xx is an error response.
monitorProxyAuth: The proxy requires authentication (HTTP 407); no login credentials were sent.
monitorIcmpNoReply: No Ping replies were received. This alone does not prove disconnection; try a web check.
monitorHttpNoReply: No HTTPS response was received; check the target, selected route and proxy status.
siteTitle: Why does this website fail to open?
siteIntro: Compare system DNS, IPv4 / IPv6 connections and two web request routes to narrow down the cause.
siteInputError: Enter a valid domain or HTTP / HTTPS address without a username or password.
siteScope: Checks the site's root page only, ignoring the path and query. No login or page content download; failures never trigger automatic network changes.
siteNoAddress: No address for this family; skipped
siteLimit: A connection or HTTP response only confirms that probe's result. Check content, login and regional restrictions in a browser.
siteBothPaths2xx: Both web routes returned 2xx. If the browser still fails, check its own proxy, extensions or login state.
siteDirectPath2xx: The request ignoring the system proxy returned 2xx. The system proxy route did not; check proxy or VPN routing.
siteWindowsProxyPath2xx: The system proxy route returned 2xx while the direct route did not. Access may depend on the existing proxy.
siteProxyAuthenticationRequired: The proxy requires authentication. This tool did not send login credentials.
siteHttpAccessRestricted: The site or an intermediary returned an access restriction. This does not prove the computer is offline.
siteHttpRedirectReceived: A redirect was received. The tool did not follow it; check the destination in a browser.
siteHttpServerErrorReceived: A server error response was received. It may come from a proxy or intermediary, so the computer is not established as the cause.
siteHttpClientErrorReceived: A request error response was received. Check the site's policy or root page address.
siteTlsValidationOrHandshakeFailed: TLS negotiation or certificate validation failed. Check the clock, certificates and proxy. Certificate checks are never bypassed.
siteHttpResponseReceived: An HTTP response was received; usable page content has not been confirmed.
siteTcpConnectedHttpUnconfirmed: At least one IP connection was established, but web success is unconfirmed. TLS, proxy or site policy may be involved.
siteSystemDnsUnconfirmed: System DNS resolution is unconfirmed. Split routing or remote proxy resolution may be involved; this does not establish a site-wide or Internet outage.
siteSiteConnectivityUnconfirmed: These results are insufficient to identify a cause. Compare network diagnostics, other sites and another device.
recoveryTitle: A previous operation may be incomplete
recoveryHint: An unfinished operation record was found. Run diagnostics before deciding whether to restore its saved configuration. No automatic rollback will occur.
recoveryReadError: Could not read recovery records; check backups under Restore configuration.
stepNotRestorable: Transient state cannot be restored exactly
repairStepCount: Completed {0} / {1} steps; review the individual results below.
repairBackupSaved: A backup was saved. Restorable settings can be recovered from repair history.
feedbackPreviewTitle: Redacted report preview · confirm to choose where to save
helpIntro: These steps are not executed automatically. Review the evidence before changing settings whose purpose you understand.
helpCableBody: Check both ends and the link lights of an Ethernet cable. For Wi-Fi, confirm the intended network. If every device on the same router is offline, check the router and broadband connection.
helpVpnTitle: No connection after closing a VPN
helpVpnBody: Start the original VPN or proxy client, disconnect normally, exit it, then rerun diagnostics. Repair only items with clear residual evidence; a company network may require its proxy settings.
helpDnsBody: Compare system DNS with actual responses from known resolvers. DNS comparison does not use the HTTP proxy, and timeouts may reflect network policy. Check why custom DNS was configured before changing it.
helpPortalBody: Look for a network sign-in prompt and verify the hotel, campus or public network's login page in a browser. Interpret authentication failures and weak signal in the local context.
helpRestoreTitle: Problems after a repair or unexpected exit
helpRestoreBody: Run diagnostics, review before/after results and each step, then select the appropriate backup. DNS cache and DHCP leases are transient and cannot be restored exactly. Save your work before any required restart.
startupFailed: Startup did not complete. Review the error and check the fully extracted files.
currentItemRepairHint: Only selected actions for this check will run, after revalidation and backup.
currentItemNoActions: No repair action is available for this check.
updateIntro: Check this project's stable GitHub release, then open its download page. No automatic installation or report upload.
updateRepositoryHint: Official default: shangguanyiyu0011/NetworkRescue. You may enter another owner/repo; blank uses the official source.
updateNotConfigured: Updates have not been checked. A request is sent only when you click Check updates.
updateAvailable: A newer stable version is available. Open its release page for details.
updateUpToDate: No newer stable release was found.
updateNoPublishedRelease: No public stable release was found. Check that the repository has a published release.
updateRateLimited: GitHub has temporarily limited requests. Check again later.
updateCheckFailed: The update check did not complete. Check the repository, network and proxy, then try again.
feedbackIntro: Send problems or suggestions to the address below.
feedbackHint: Include the app version, Windows version, steps to reproduce and a redacted report. Review it before sharing; exclude passwords, subscriptions and keys.
useHelpBeginnerBody:
Use this when you suddenly cannot get online and want to find the cause.
1. Click Start diagnosis and wait for the eight checks.
2. Read the conclusion and advice. Select applicable repairs before clicking One-click repair.
3. When the network is healthy, Save as healthy snapshot creates a dated snapshot. Compare settings later in Settings.
useHelpAdvancedTitle: Advanced mode: review evidence and choose actions
useHelpAdvancedBody:
Use this to inspect evidence or investigate a specific issue.
1. Select a check and read its conclusion and evidence on the right. Expand raw records when needed.
2. Select applicable actions and click the item's repair button. Changes still require confirmation and backup.
3. Filter active connections by program, PID, address, or state. Process names describe the sampling time, not historical ownership.
useHelpMonitoringBody: Observe intermittent non-responses or latency changes. Enter 1–4 hostnames or IPs, choose methods, interval and count, then start manually. HTTPS may follow the system proxy for VPNs; unanswered Ping is not proof of an outage. Encrypted local history saves every 15 seconds and on finish/close, with up to 20 sessions and 64 MiB total, available after restarting and for export.
useHelpSpeedBody:
Use this to measure the connection to the current test node.
1. Choose direct access or the system proxy and start the test. It uses download and upload traffic.
2. Download and upload run in sequence. You can stop; unfinished phases have no final result.
3. Hover near a line or node to see the actual sample's phase time and average speed. This does not guarantee your ISP access bandwidth.
useHelpReportBody:
You can export a report whether diagnosis is healthy or finds an issue.
1. Click Export report, review the redacted preview, and choose a local save location.
2. Export existing monitoring observations after stopping. Repair history is in Settings.
3. Check again before sharing. Do not include passwords, subscriptions, keys, or personal data. Reports are not uploaded automatically.
adapterReadError: Some information could not be read.
speedChartHint: Lines show interval rates from actual transferred bytes. Final metrics use completed phases; stopping preserves the chart.
speedChartEmpty: Download and upload lines appear when data transfers begin.
speedResultNote: Results describe the connection to this test node.
connectionsEmpty: No active TCP connections were found.
speedAverageChartHint: Uses the same calculation as the results above: successfully completed bytes divided by elapsed phase time. Download and upload run in sequence.
speedPhaseSeconds: Time within each phase (seconds; measured in sequence)
speedAverageEmpty: The average-speed chart appears after a transfer completes successfully.
specialNoRepairNeeded: This check passed; no repair is needed.
specialRepairUnavailable: No repair is supported by clear evidence. Review the check results.
specialSelectRepair: Choose a repair for this check.
siteNoIpv6Explanation: The target returned no IPv6 address for this test, so this connection was not tested. Consider the IPv4 and web-check results.
siteRedirectExplanation: The website responded and requested a redirect. This tool did not open the next page, so it has not verified whether that page will load.
siteHttpOkExplanation: The website responded. This test checked the connection and response headers without loading the page content.
siteDirectExplanation: This request ignores the Windows HTTP proxy settings. A VPN tunnel may still affect the connection.
siteProxyExplanation: This request follows the current Windows HTTP proxy rules, which may also select a direct connection for this website. A VPN tunnel may still affect the connection.
appearanceHint: Choose a theme that suits your lighting.
freeUseBody: The official software is free to use. We do not sell activation codes or charge a usage-license fee.
openSourcePending: This project is open source under the GNU GPL v3 (GPL-3.0-only) license. Source code: https://github.com/shangguanyiyu0011/NetworkRescue
reportFakeSales: If someone impersonates the official project to sell this software or charge for activation, report it to the feedback email or the relevant marketplace.
reportSalesHint: You may include a sales link or screenshot to help verify the report.
monitorTargetsIntro: Compare 1–4 targets with separate HTTPS response or ICMP latency statistics.
monitorSessionPrivacy: Monitoring starts manually and observes settings read-only, saving encrypted local records every 15 seconds and on finish/close. Up to 20 sessions and 64 MiB total; no resident background service or upload. Encryption is not anonymization.
monitorGatewayUnknown: No configured gateway was available to add.
monitorTargetsInputError: Enter a valid domain or IP address for every target and check the interval and sample count.
monitorTimelineHint: Tracks target response loss/recovery and proxy, DNS, IP, configured gateway, and adapter changes. No response does not prove an outage. Select cells to copy.
monitorTimelineEmpty: Session events appear after monitoring starts.
monitorTimelineTruncated: Only the latest 500 events are retained; earlier events were truncated. The full event count is shown above.
monitorEventTargetNoResponse: Target did not respond (not proof of an outage)
monitorEventObservationUnavailable: Settings could not be read; this does not indicate removal
monitorSessionFailed: Monitoring did not complete. Existing observations remain available to view or export.
healthProfilesHint: Save a configuration snapshot within 5 minutes of a healthy diagnosis. Comparison lists configuration differences only; it does not diagnose faults or restore settings.
healthProfilesEmpty: No healthy snapshots have been saved.
healthProfileGate: Run a healthy diagnosis first. Diagnose again if settings change or more than 5 minutes pass.
healthComparisonNone: No confirmed configuration differences were found.
healthComparisonPartial: Some settings could not be read. Unknown values do not indicate removal.
profileNameError: Enter a non-empty name of 1–64 characters.
profileLimitHint: Save up to 20 entries. Delete an old entry when the limit is reached.
monitorPlansHint: Save the settings above if you often check the same targets. You can start monitoring without saving.
monitorPlansEmpty: Nothing saved yet. Enter your targets above, then save the settings if you want to reuse them.
monitorPlanInvalid: This plan has invalid targets or sampling parameters. Current controls were not changed.
monitorReplayHint: Select an event in the current or a saved session to inspect nearby real samples and configuration changes. Loading history starts no network checks and does not reconstruct missing observations.
monitorReplayEmpty: Select a timeline event to replay.
monitorReplayNoSample: No retained sample is near this time. Up to 3600 actual samples per target are retained; the chart shows the latest 300 points. Missing network states cannot be inferred.
monitorReplayWindow: Samples are searched within one interval of the event (at least 2 seconds). Configuration changes include recorded events within 10 seconds.
monitorReplayNoResponse: No response (not proof of an outage)
monitorReplayNoConfiguration: No retained configuration change events are near this time.
connectionSearch: Search address, port, PID, or program
connectionFilteredEmpty: No connections match the search and state filter.
connectionTruncated: Connection results were truncated. Filters apply only to captured records.
connectionReadUnavailable: Some connection information could not be read. Empty or unknown values do not prove there are no connections.
healthConfigurationChanged: Network settings changed or could not be fully read. Diagnose again before saving a healthy snapshot.
workspaceDeletePrompt: Delete the selected saved item? This removes the local record without changing network settings.
workspaceDuplicateName: This name is already in use. Choose another name.
workspaceLimit: You can save up to 20 snapshots and 20 plans. Delete an unused item first.
workspaceNotFound: This saved item was not found. Refresh the list and try again.
workspaceInvalid: The name or plan settings are invalid. Check them and try again.
workspaceUnavailable: Local data could not be read or saved. Existing data was not overwritten. Check disk space and access permissions, then try again.
healthComparisonTruncated: Many changes were found. Showing the first {0} of {1}.
monitorPlanNameExample: For example: Home network, Office network, VPN checks
monitorPlanUseHint: Choosing settings fills the controls above. Click Start monitoring when you are ready.
monitorPlanSaved: Saved “{0}”. Next time, choose it here and click Start monitoring.
healthSnapshotSaved: Healthy snapshot saved: {0}. View and compare it in Settings.
faultMetricLegend: Values show successful / attempted checks. An unsuccessful check alone does not mean the computer is offline.
useHelpSnapshotsBody:
Save working settings so you can compare them when trouble occurs.
1. After a healthy diagnosis, Save as healthy snapshot uses the date and time. Repeated saves in the same second get a number.
2. Choose a snapshot under Settings → Healthy snapshots and compare it with current settings. Manual names are also available there.
3. Save up to 20 snapshots. Saving requires a healthy diagnosis within 5 minutes and unchanged settings. Comparison lists differences; it does not restore settings or declare every change a fault.
useHelpMonitorPlansTitle: Saved monitoring settings: reuse your setup
useHelpMonitorPlansBody:
Use this if you often check the same targets. Saving is optional.
1. Fill in the targets, methods, proxy routes, interval, and count on Monitoring.
2. Expand Saved monitoring settings, enter a name, and save the settings above. Keep up to 20 sets.
3. Choosing a saved set fills the controls. You must still click Start monitoring. Saved sets contain parameters, not test results.
useHelpReplayBody: Select timeline events to inspect nearby real samples, other targets and configuration changes. Retain up to 3600 samples per target, latest 300 chart points and 500 events with truncation indicated. Saved sessions replay across restarts. Interrupted sessions restore the last checkpoint; up to 15 seconds of samples may be missing. Nearby events do not prove causation; missing data cannot be reconstructed, and damaged records are not overwritten or deleted.
monitorCurveNoResponseLegend: Bottom dot: no valid response for that sample
monitorCurveMeaning: The line breaks when a sample has no response. This does not mean 0 ms or prove that the computer is offline.
monitorHistoryHint: The 20 latest monitoring sessions saved on this PC. Loading replays saved observations without starting network checks.
monitorHistoryReadError: Monitoring history could not be read. Refresh to retry; damaged records are preserved.
monitorReplayUnrecovered: Recovery unconfirmed at the last observation
siteFamilyExplanation: Bypasses the system proxy and forces resolved addresses in this family, retaining the original hostname and default TLS validation. At most 2 addresses and 3 seconds total per family.
siteFamilyNoAddress: DNS returned no address in this family; this check is not applicable.
siteFamilyDnsUnconfirmed: DNS results are unconfirmed, so HTTP was not checked for this family.
siteFamilyNoResponse: No HTTP response was confirmed from the attempted addresses. This does not establish failure of the entire protocol or all addresses and will not automatically disable a protocol.
siteAddressFamilyHttpPartialFailure: HTTP response unconfirmed for one address family
portalLoginTitle: This network may require web sign-in
portalLoginHint: Opens the Windows connectivity trigger page in the system browser. The network may redirect to sign-in; this is not a confirmed portal and does not sign in automatically. Run diagnostics again afterward.
monitorHistoryDeleteConfirm: Delete the selected local monitoring record? Network settings will not change.
monitorHistoryClearConfirm: Clear all readable local monitoring records? Damaged or unreadable records are preserved; network settings will not change.
monitorHistorySaveError: Monitoring could not be saved. Existing files will not be overwritten. Check disk space and access permissions.
monitorHistoryMissing: The selected record is missing or unreadable. Refresh history; damaged files will not be overwritten or deleted.
monitorHistoryPrivacy: After you manually start monitoring, records are automatically encrypted for the current user and saved locally, never uploaded. Saves occur every 15 seconds and on finish/close. Limits: 20 sessions, 64 MiB total, 3600 samples per target, latest 300 chart points and 500 events. Interrupted sessions restore the last checkpoint; up to 15 seconds of samples may be missing.
portalLoginUnavailable: No network sign-in trigger is available. Run diagnostics again.
portalLoginConfirm: Open the Windows connectivity trigger page in the system browser? This is not a confirmed portal and the network may redirect it. No automatic sign-in will occur.
speedLatencyHint: Compare actual latency observations while idle, downloading and uploading. Statistics remain blank when samples are insufficient; results describe this probe path.
qualityTimeAxis: X axis: actual sample time; gaps indicate missing observations.
wifiStabilityHint: Reads the current Wi-Fi interface only during manual monitoring. Signal and negotiated link rates are not Internet speed measurements. Network names and access-point identifiers are not recorded.
wifiAccessDenied: Wi-Fi interface access is restricted; this does not establish disconnection.
wifiReplayHint: Shows real Wi-Fi observations around the selected event; missing samples are not filled.
wifiNoSamples: No Wi-Fi samples in this time window.
dnsQualityHint: Repeats A and AAAA queries for the same domain for the selected number of rounds. Results describe this limited observation and do not automatically change system DNS.
dnsQualityInputError: Choose 3–10 rounds and specify 1–4 DNS servers.
dnsQualityNoRecords: Answered with no records of this type
dnsQualityLimited: Limited observations; answer changes may reflect normal DNS load balancing.
wifiHistoryUnsupported: This version of the historical record did not collect Wi-Fi observations.
wifiTruncated: Only the latest 720 Wi-Fi observations were retained; evidence for earlier times may be missing.
dnsQualityRoundDuration: Total A + AAAA duration per round
dnsQualityRatesHint: Rates use completed rounds only: any valid A/AAAA reply counts as a response round; any NOERROR reply containing an address counts as resolved; any timed-out query counts as a timeout round. Categories can overlap. Unfinished rounds on cancellation are excluded.
